notes: The 1985 text does not list which libraries are 'available'; it names a library by the role it plays in a compilation: a library-name 'names a COBOL library that is to be used by the compiler for a given source program compilation' (III.2), and library-names may be referenced 'provided that the compiling system supports the associated library' (X.1.3.8). A directory the library place holds but no COPY of the compilation names is not a library used for that compilation, so the compiler's set (the default library plus each library a COPY of the group names that a place holds; docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-40.md, 'The libraries available during a compilation') is the reading the definition supports, and its counting is probed both ways (an unqualified COPY before or after a named library refused COBOL0900; a named library no place holds is CBL3620 and not counted). Reading B (every subdirectory of a library place is available) gives a directory listing the force of a source rule; the text gives it none. Beyond the definition the set is the implementor's, which the compiler documents; GnuCOBOL 3.2 -std=cobol85 accepts onlyunq.cob too (probe this session), and enforces no qualification at all.
